displayPattern: Washer display shows bE2 (also shown as E2, 6E2, BE2 or 8E2 on some models)
meaning: Jammed button error: a button on the control panel is detected as stuck or continuously pressed.
causes: A control panel button stuck or held in
On some models BE2 (8E2) is a MEMS sensor error instead, not a jammed button
diySteps: Touch every button on the panel one at a time, working each one back and forth to reach all its edges before releasing it
Power the washer back on and check whether the code has cleared

If your display shows BE2 or 8E2, check your user manual: on some models that is a MEMS sensor error. Samsung's basic steps for it are to power off for 2 to 3 minutes, power back on and restart the cycle
safetyNote: Unplug the washer (or switch off its breaker) and close the water taps before you reach behind it, handle hoses or open a filter. Water left from a recent hot cycle can be very hot, so let it cool first. Never bypass the door lock. Motor, pump, valve, sensor and control-board repairs belong to a qualified appliance technician.
proAdvice: If any button is damaged, or the code returns after you power the washer back on, Samsung says to request service.
sourceTitle: Samsung washing machine information and error codes (Samsung Support)
